title: The obstruction concerns global affine directions after coefficients are supplied
statement: Given explicit homogeneous cubic with integer coefficients, deciding existence of nonzero d such that P(x+td) is affine for EVERY x is NP-hard. Homogenized 3-SAT quadratics q_j(v) encode Boolean/auxiliary variables and clauses. P(w,z,v)=w^3+3w||z||^2+sum z_jq_j(v) has nonnegative w derivative3(w^2+||z||^2), preventing spurious auxiliary zero directions; gradient zeros exactly encode nonzero common q zeros. D_d^2P(x)=2 gradP(d)^T x. For N Boolean+auxiliary variables, YES has unit d with gradP(d)=0; NO every unit d satisfies||gradP(d)||>1/(384N). Rounding residuals<=1/(192N) recovers satisfying assignment, giving polynomial dimensions/bitlength/reciprocal gap. Gaussian-base expected squared directional curvature is4||gradP(d)||^2. This is specifically GLOBAL AFFINE-DIRECTION RECOGNITION, not hardness of every approximate representation learner, adaptive policy, sensing optimum or total read count. One affine direction need not save a read. Hillar–Lim context is adjacent, not substitute proof or novelty.
